status: Fictional independent cases. Labels written on 14 November 2026 by a lane that had not read the phrase rules, without running the rules on them, and awaiting the owner's review.
authorship: The author read PRODUCT.md, the structure and action names of cue-rules-held-out.json, and the description of what a held-out case is. During unrelated demo work the author had also read the browser preview's demo stand-in (src/lib/preview.ts), and saw the opening cases of the held-out file while reading its structure. The engine's rules and their written descriptions were not read.
replay: Same format as cue-rules-held-out.json: lines arrive in order with one speaker label. Where a case has an existingCue, that cue is on screen after its source line. userName, when present, is the session-only name from Settings.

actions.quiet: Nothing should change: no new cue, and a cue on screen stays as it is.
actions.withdraw: The cue on screen should be removed because it is stale or unwanted.
actions.resolved: The cue on screen has been answered by the conversation.

events.text: The hall gave us forty chairs, but they are all still stacked in the storeroom.
Right, and somebody has to get those out before the doors open on Saturday.

expected.reason: Getting the chairs out is a task with a time attached and nobody named to do it.

events.text: The server cupboard still has to be emptied before the movers turn up.
Yeah. It's mostly old cables and a printer nobody uses.

expected.reason: Emptying the cupboard is needed before the move and no one has taken it.

events.text: Lena's running the tombola, so that one's covered.
No, wait, Lena's away that weekend. So the tombola hasn't got anybody.

expected.reason: The correction removes the only owner, leaving the tombola without one.

events.text: We still need a person on the gate for the morning shift.
I'll do the gate, I'm there from eight anyway.

existingCue.text: Who will take the gate in the morning?

expected.reason: A speaker takes the gate shift in the next line.

events.text: The compost bins want turning, and no one has touched them since June.
They do, they're starting to smell.
Leave that with me. I can do it Sunday morning.

existingCue.text: Who will turn the compost bins?

expected.reason: Two lines later a speaker takes the job and says when.

events.text: We've got to get the street-closure form in to the parish office at some point fairly soon.

expected.reason: The form has a deadline in spirit but no date.

events.text: I'll send the floor plan over to the movers once I get a minute.
Great, they keep asking for it.

expected.reason: Others are waiting on the floor plan and the promise has no time.

events.text: Let's have the stall list finished nice and early this time.
And by early I mean Thursday at noon, before the newsletter goes out.

existingCue.text: When does the stall list need to be finished?

expected.reason: The next line turns "early" into a day and time.

events.text: We ought to get the seed order in before too long.
The catalogue price only holds until the end of the month, mind.
Then let's order on the twentieth.

existingCue.text: What date should the seed order go in?

expected.reason: The group settles on the twentieth two lines later.

events.text: So that's the budget done.
Maren, could you tell us how many tables the cake stall wants?

expected.reason: Maren is asked a direct question by name.

events.text: I think the van is sorted, but what did the landlord say about using the lift, Tobias?

expected.reason: The question is put to Tobias, with his name at the end.

events.text: Maren did the posters last year and they were lovely.
They really were. People kept them.

expected.reason: Maren is mentioned and thanked, not asked anything.

events.text: As Maren said earlier, the hall's booked from ten, so we can set up from then.

expected.reason: The listener is quoted, not addressed, and nothing is open.

events.text: Idris, do you know whether the big urn still works?

expected.reason: The question is for Idris, not for Maren.

events.text: Hana, can you check with Tobias's team afterwards and tell me how many desks they need?

expected.reason: Hana is the one asked; Tobias's name appears only as whose team it is.

events.text: Does anyone know if we still have the gazebo, or did it go in the skip?

expected.reason: The question goes to the whole room, so it is not clearly for the listener.

events.text: The cash tin is in the school office.
Could you grab the float from there on Friday?

expected.reason: Nothing says who "you" is, so it cannot be treated as asked of the listener.

events.text: Nobody's down to collect the keys from the caretaker yet.
The bunting's in my boot, by the way.
Like I say, we still haven't got anyone collecting those keys.

existingCue.text: Who will collect the keys from the caretaker?

expected.reason: The same gap is restated; the question already showing covers it.

events.text: That risk form needs to go to the council soon.
Honestly, it really does need to go in soon.

existingCue.text: When does the risk form need to go in?

expected.reason: The second line only repeats the first, adding no date and no new point.

events.text: Somebody has to ring the bouncy castle people.
Anyway, moving on to parking. The field's waterlogged.
We might have to ask for the school car park.

existingCue.text: Who will ring the bouncy castle people?

expected.reason: The meeting has moved on to parking and stays there.

events.text: It's either the blue carpet tiles or the grey ones.
The other thing about the grey is that it hides coffee.

existingCue.text: How will you choose between the blue and grey tiles?

expected.reason: Still weighing the same two options; "the other thing" is not a new subject.

events.text: We could hire a skip, or do tip runs with Yusuf's trailer.
Tip runs are a faff, to be fair.
Let's just go with the skip, then. Settled.

existingCue.text: How will you choose between the skip and the trailer?

expected.reason: The choice is made two lines later.

events.text: We should fix a date for the autumn work party at some stage.
Let's park that until we've seen what the weather does, and come back to it in September.

existingCue.text: What date should the autumn work party be?

expected.reason: The group puts the date off on purpose, so asking for it now is unwanted.

events.text: What colour are we painting the new shed, green or that dark blue?
Let's not get into that tonight. It's on the agenda for March.

existingCue.text: How will you choose between green and dark blue?

expected.reason: The choice is deferred to a named later meeting.

events.text: The move is coming up, so we need the crates packed in good time.
Sorry, scrap that. Facilities have just told me our floor isn't moving at all.

existingCue.text: When do the crates need to be packed?

expected.reason: The speaker takes the whole thing back, so there is nothing to time.

events.text: Someone needs to book the minibus for the trip to the seed swap.
Oh, hang on, I'm wrong. Farah booked it last week, it's on the sheet.

expected.reason: The speaker corrects themselves: the booking is done and has a name on it.

events.text: The tomatoes went mad this year.
We had three crates off the end bed alone.

expected.reason: Small talk about the harvest; nothing is open.

events.text: I'll bring the extension lead on Friday, and Wes is fetching the urn at nine.

expected.reason: Both jobs have a person and a time.

events.text: Thanks, everyone, for coming out in this rain.
Tea's in the pot if anybody wants one.

expected.reason: A welcome and an offer of tea.

events.text: Who'd have thought a cake stall could make four hundred pounds?
I know. Absolutely brilliant.

expected.reason: A rhetorical question that nobody is expected to answer.

events.text: We went with the green T-shirts in the end, and they turned up yesterday.

expected.reason: Reports a choice already made and delivered.

events.text: Somebody had already swept the hall by the time I got there, which was nice.

expected.reason: Describes something already done; it is not a job waiting for an owner.

events.text: When's the skip coming? Oh, it's on the sheet. Tuesday the fourth.

expected.reason: The speaker answers their own question in the same breath.

events.text: The new office has those windows that actually open.
And a kettle on every floor, apparently.

expected.reason: Chat about the new office; no task, date, choice or question.
